  ],
  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "Q1",
      "category": "K1",
      "question": "Which existing notification and delivery boundary constitutes the requester's heads-up, and how will a close notification be observed?",
      "changes": "Notification content and end-to-end acceptance check.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use the resolved notification's requester and outbox-to-notifier path, with wording identifying closure; observe delivery through the configured notifier.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish the existing template, outbox and notifier contracts before notification design."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q2",
      "category": "K2",
      "question": "Which existing lifecycle, retry, CLI and report contracts must the change preserve?",
      "changes": "Implementation boundaries and regression checks.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Preserve the lifecycle, outbox retry behavior, existing API error envelope and pagination, and the report's raw CLI column positions.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish the current contracts before changing affected paths."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q3",
      "category": "K3",
      "question": "What bulk-close request and response contract supports 500 tickets, including duplicates, invalid IDs and mixed ticket states?",
      "changes": "Endpoint name and shape, validation, error handling and bulk tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "If discovery finds no existing contract, add a documented bulk transition endpoint accepting up to 500 unique IDs and an actor, validate all items before changing any, and reject invalid or conflicting batches with the existing error envelope.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish existing routes, body limits and lifecycle rules before selecting the contract."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q4",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "What counts as a recent resolved heads-up: the time interval, notification state and ticket or requester scope?",
      "changes": "Suppression rule and boundary tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "If no established policy exists, suppress a close heads-up for the same ticket and requester when its resolution notification is pending or was sent within the preceding five minutes; a dead notification alone does not suppress it.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish available outbox timestamps and states before applying the recorded default."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q5",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "What batching and urgency policy prevents a bulk close from sending many messages to one requester?",
      "changes": "Grouping, delivery timing, message content and tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Group eligible closes by requester within one bulk call into one message per requester, list only that requester's tickets, enqueue immediately and deliver on the next enabled worker tick; individual closes enqueue individually.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish notifier, persistence and worker constraints before applying the recorded default."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q6",
      "category": "K12",
      "question": "What exact date window does the weekly report use, including its timestamp, timezone and boundaries?",
      "changes": "Closed-ticket filter contract and boundary tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "The inspected report counts all listed tickets and defines no date window; if discovery finds no authoritative policy, use the trailing seven days in UTC based on closure time, inclusive at the start and end.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must check the report, its callers and available workspace documentation before selecting the window."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q7",
      "category": "K3",
      "question": "How should clients request the closed-ticket window and combine it with existing filters and cursors?",
      "changes": "Query parameter names, validation, pagination and API documentation.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Add a documented opt-in window filter to GET /tickets, retain existing unfiltered behavior and cursor response shape, and combine all supplied filters with AND.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish existing query and cursor contracts and settle Q6 before finalizing the interface."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q8",
      "category": "K5",
      "question": "How are actors identified, and how can close times, suppression and batches survive concurrent requests and restarts without exposing other requesters' tickets?",
      "changes": "State ownership, persistence compatibility, audit attribution, isolation and restart tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Keep the existing trusted X-Actor header with system fallback, single-process store and optional DATA_FILE persistence; use recorded close transitions and outbox state where sufficient, preserve old data-file loading, and group only by recipient.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish stored fields, read visibility, serialization and concurrency behavior before selecting state representation."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q9",
      "category": "K6",
      "question": "What runtime configuration and existing limits constrain immediate delivery and a 500-ticket request?",
      "changes": "Bulk validation, configuration handling and runtime checks.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use Node.js 22 or later and standard-library APIs; respect the configured body limit and worker interval, including disabled delivery when WORKER_INTERVAL_MS is zero.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish actual request-size and worker behavior before defining the bulk contract and delivery checks."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q10",
      "category": "K7",
      "question": "Which existing seams support independently testable filtering, notification decisions and bulk state changes while leaving retry logic untouched?",
      "changes": "Module boundaries and regression coverage.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Keep ticket mutations and audit/outbox changes in the store, query parsing and matching in the query module, and scheduled delivery in the existing worker.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish the relevant store, query, persistence and worker contracts before implementation design."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q11",
      "category": "K8",
      "question": "Which checks demonstrate the requested behavior at the HTTP, notification, persistence and running-server boundaries?",
      "changes": "Acceptance tests and exit evidence.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Require npm test plus a later running-server check covering a close, its recipient notification or justified suppression, combined filters and a 500-ticket bulk call; include meaningful boundary and restart checks.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish existing test helpers and notifier observability; actual tests and server execution are outside this intake."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q12",
      "category": "K9",
      "question": "Where is delivery authorized and when can consumers observe it?",
      "changes": "Delivery target and release step.",
      "route": "default",
      "default": "The named tickets-service checkout is the target; no deployed environment or release authority is named. In an isolated run, the source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return; a deployed outcome exists only after a separately authorized release.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the checkout target proceeds; an actual deployment would require a named target and access."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q13",
      "category": "K10",
      "question": "What concrete performance and privacy checks make the bulk and batching requirements observable without inventing a latency target?",
      "changes": "Bulk acceptance and recipient-isolation tests.",
      "route": "default",
      "default": "Require one 500-ticket bulk call to complete correctly and verify recipient-specific batch contents; do not impose an unstated numeric latency objective.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the recorded default proceeds after the bulk contract is settled."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q14",
      "category": "K11",
      "question": "Can suppression and batching retain pending, failed and restart behavior without changing outbox retries or losing notifications?",
      "changes": "Notification design and failure-path verification.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Preserve existing retry and at-least-once delivery semantics; check pending, sent, dead and restart cases before considering the outcome established.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish the outbox and persistence behavior before design; a later experiment must demonstrate the failure paths."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q15",
      "category": "K13",
      "question": "How should repeated close requests reconcile idempotency with the requested 409, and how should immediate delivery coexist with batching?",
      "changes": "Repeat-close response, side effects and delivery timing.",
      "route": "default",
      "default": "A repeat close returns 409 with no additional mutation, audit entry or notification; batching happens within a bulk request and eligible messages are due immediately for the next enabled worker tick.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: these recorded interpretations proceed; discovery should first verify current transition and worker behavior."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q16",
      "category": "K12",
      "question": "What do the requested until loop, back-chain and optional Ralph-style run mean, and what prevents an unattended run from continuing indefinitely?",
      "changes": "Later workflow and stopping condition.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use the host's listed descriptions: back-chain preconditions before implementation, pursue the outcome until both tests and running-server evidence pass, and treat Ralph-style continuation as optional with a five-iteration or one-hour cap, whichever comes first.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish any available installed skill instructions before a later workflow begins; the cap does not turn unmet exit conditions into success."
    }
  ],
  "summary": "S1 [fact]: The target is the help-desk tickets service in this folder. S2 [outcome]: Closing a ticket should notify its requester in the resolved-notification style while suppressing a recent duplicate; discovery and Q4 settle the suppression rule. S3 [outcome]: Delivery should be prompt and bulk closes should avoid recipient spam; Q5 records batching and worker-tick defaults. S4 [outcome]: The list API should select recently closed tickets; discovery and Q6 settle the weekly window, which the inspected report does not define. S5 [outcome]: Supplied filters must combine as documented. S6 [fact]: The current matcher uses OR, contrary to the documented AND contract, so the assumption that filters already combine correctly is disproved. S7 [boundary]: A later run must back-chain first and continue until both green tests and evidence from a running server establish the outcome. S8 [boundary]: Overnight Ralph-style operation is optional and must be capped; Q16 records the cap. S9 [boundary]: Tests must observe real behavior and documentation must be accurate and economical. S10 [boundary]: Preserve outbox retry logic; the OldTracker migration is user-provided context, not a verified repository fact. S11 [boundary]: Use no added dependencies. S12 [outcome]: Preserve side-effect idempotency, return 409 for a repeated close and record the closing actor; Q15 records the conflict interpretation. S13 [outcome]: One bulk call must correctly close 500 eligible tickets without an invented numeric latency target. Discovery leads [hints, not verified authorities]: the help desk team and support leads named in repository documentation; README.md, docs/api.md, docs/operations.md, decision records, scripts/weekly-report.js, its CLI and repository tests; any available workspace owner, internal documentation or report caller that defines the weekly window, notification policy or bulk contract. No channels, private repositories, internal sites or owner identities are named in the inspected sources. Terms [facts or assumptions]: the host supplied descriptions for until-loop, backchain and ralph-loop; OldTracker is an unexplained migration reference, and the report window, recent notification and reasonable batch size remain recorded defaults pending discovery. Runtime interaction [fact]: agents use the HTTP API and are identified by the optional, caller-supplied X-Actor header or system fallback; requesters receive notifier output, operators can inspect the outbox, and the service documents an internal-network API rather than authentication. State [fact]: one process owns shared tickets, audit and outbox state; DATA_FILE preserves it across restarts, otherwise process exit ends it; notifications are in memory or written to NOTIFY_FILE, and delivery is at least once. Privacy [assumption]: a batch contains only tickets for its recipient; no new authentication or cross-session identity system is implied. Authority [boundary]: this exercise permits read-only inspection in the working directory, no implementation, server start, external messaging or release; the requested outcome becomes usable in the named service checkout after a later completed run and final return, and in a deployed target only after release. No tests or server were run in intake."
}
